call_points.text: Store guidance reiterated: over 60 new restaurants in FY27 and 580 to 630 restaurants by December 2027.
SSSG was 4.3% for the quarter, positive in all three months, with May and June at mid-single digit.
Growth was footfall-led: on-premise rose 12% and off-premise 11% YoY, with double-digit guest count growth.
Over 200 bps of inflation across fuel, food, packaging, wages and utilities was absorbed by cost governance and operating leverage.
Gross margin at 67.6% was stable YoY; management calls this the peak of the inflation impact and expects improvement from here.
No price increase has been taken yet this year; the company typically takes about 3% a year.
The board approved an interim dividend of ₹0.40 per equity share.
Operating structure is being realigned from three divisions to five to bring execution closer to the customer.
Asked which cost line hurt most, management named food, paper and distribution plus utilities as the largest, with wages and advertising also higher.
Asked for pre-Ind AS margins, the CEO deferred to the presentation rather than giving the figure on the call.
Gross margins guided to remain sustainable around the 67% level.
Guest count growth reached mid-single digits, a key focus for volume recovery.
On track for Vision 2027 target of 580-630 restaurants.
Coffee subscription launched at ₹55 for 10 visits to drive McCafé loyalty.
Targeting ₹3,000 Cr annual revenue as the next major milestone.
South India guest count turned positive for the first time in several quarters.
Targeting 60+ new restaurant openings in FY27, up from 48 in FY26.
Near-term gross margins expected to remain in the +67% range.
Digital sales contribution reached 76%, led by McDelivery and the app.
Inflation in cocoa and coffee mitigated through supply chain efficiencies.
On track to reach 580-630 restaurants by 2027.
Ranked 6th globally in the Restaurants & Leisure Facilities sector for sustainability.
